Highlight Clip: CleanSpark CBO: Power Access Will Be Bitcoin Miners' Key Competitive Advantage CleanSpark CBO: Power Access Will Be Bitcoin Miners' Key Competitive Advantage CleanSpark CBO Harry Sudock told What Bitcoin Did on November 5 that if starting a company today, he'd build an energy business first, then decide whether its power would serve Bitcoin mining or AI. CleanSpark measures its business in megawatt-hours, megawatts, and acres, with AI data centers offering a way to realize their value. Bitcoin miners can adjust electricity consumption based on prices or contracts, while AI data centers manage grid balancing differently. Sudock sees transmission, not generation, as the main US power-grid bottleneck, requiring further investment in transmission and distribution alongside solar, natural gas, and nuclear power. — link

Bloomberg: Trump Memecoin Dinner Returns as Demand Falls and Political Scrutiny Rises Donald Trump is set to attend another dinner for top TRUMP memecoin holders as participation declines sharply and the token trades about 99% below its 2025 peak. Crypto trader Morten Christensen told Bloomberg that hedging his TRUMP holdings reduced his net cost of qualifying from about $1,200 for the first dinner and $500 for the second to a roughly $6 profit this time. Democratic lawmakers have renewed conflict-of-interest concerns over token holders receiving private access to the president, while the White House said the privately organized event is not a government function. — link

Highlight Clip: Coinbase CEO: AI Gives You an Infinite Team of L5-Level Employees Coinbase CEO: AI Gives You an Infinite Team of L5-Level Employees On November 18, 2026, Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said in an interview with David Senra that Coinbase's use of AI has shifted from entering prompts to assigning goals to agents, which lead teams of humans or other agents and seek input on important decisions. He believes agents can now perform at the level of L5 or L6 employees, effectively giving people access to an unlimited team of L5-level employees. He currently uses seven or eight lead agents, each responsible for a different area, coordinated by a chief-of-staff agent. Each lead agent may also deploy three to five subagents while working. — link
